description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-03) from the BA (#1028/#1032) merge-review probe battery (scratchpad p1028/fh.pl rows 6, 12, 18).  PRE-EXISTING (the whole probe file died on main before #1032; on BA's tree these are the rows still wrong).  Both emission paths.

    open(FH, '<', '/etc/passwd');
    print -f *FH;      # perl 1, PCL 0   -- a GLOB VALUE in the slot
    print -f \*FH;     # perl 1, PCL 0   -- a GLOB REF in the slot
    print -e STDOUT;   # perl 1, PCL ""  -- a STANDARD STREAM: perl fstat()s the fd; PCL has no path for it
    opendir(DIR, "/etc"); print -d DIR;   # perl 1, PCL 0 -- a DIRHANDLE (perl >= 5.10 stats the dir fd)

WHERE: `%p-stat-arg` / `%p--path` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), the ONE funnel stat/lstat/filetests go through (#1032 made the bareword reach it).  It resolves a symbol (handle NAME) and a lexical handle (stream); it does not resolve a typeglob VALUE, a glob REF, a dirhandle, or a stream with no backing path (the std streams, pipes, sockets).  perl's rule: any of those is an IO handle -> fstat(fileno).  Fix shape: one arm per kind in the funnel, and for a stream without a pathname use sb-posix:fstat on its fd (sb-sys:fd-stream-fd) instead of failing -- which also answers -s / -M on a pipe the way perl does.  Rule 12: a handle-shaped operand the funnel cannot classify must DIE naming it, not answer "" (today's answer for STDOUT is a plausible false).
Guard: rows in Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t (BA's file) for the four kinds.  Bars: cl/ change -> sweep + companion io/ + op/ (t/op/filetest.t, t/op/stat.t: 111 perl rows, 0 PCL rows today).
RELATED: #1032 (done), #1033 (errno half), #1043 (scalar-context stat), #1044 (the constant/sub-in-slot residue).


=== DONE (s470bs) ===

SHIPPED across the first two commits (runtime only).  All four kinds the task
named now resolve, and the fix is the one the task asked for â ONE arm per
kind in the funnel, none of it per-operator:

  * a glob VALUE, a glob REF and an IO ref: `%p-stat-operand` asks
    `%p-resolve-fh`, THE filehandle resolver, which has always known those
    shapes.
  * a STANDARD STREAM: the fd comes from `%p-fd-of-stream`, the reading
    `fileno` already uses, which peels a SYNONYM stream.  The old code called
    `sb-sys:fd-stream-fd` directly, which ERRORS on a synonym stream â that is
    why `-e STDOUT` was "" while `fileno(STDOUT)` was 1.
  * a DIRHANDLE: perl fstat(2)s the dirfd and PCL has none, so `opendir` now
    remembers the DIRECTORY in `*p-dirhandle-paths*`, keyed on the handle's own
    `(index . names)` cons â the object BOTH spellings hold, so one lookup
    serves `opendir DIR` and `opendir my $dh`.  `closedir` drops the entry,
    which is what makes a closed dirhandle EBADF.

RULE 12 is satisfied by the KIND dispatch: `%p--path` is an `ecase` over
:fd / :bad / :path, so an operand kind nobody handles dies naming itself
instead of answering a plausible "".

Guard rows 29-34 (glob value / glob ref / std stream) and 53-55 (dirhandle) of
`Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t`, inverse-verified against 027ba9c's runtime.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, filetest/stat operand KINDS): a GLOB VALUE `-f *FH`, a GLOB REF `-f \*FH`, a DIRHANDLE `-d DIR` and a STANDARD STREAM `-e STDOUT` all answer false in PCL where perl fstat()s the handle -- `%p-stat-arg` / `%p--path` resolve only a bareword NAME and a lexical stream with a path
